display.title: Yom Kippur and Tashlich: Why We Throw Our Sins into Moving Water
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains the Ten Days of Teshuvah leading to Yom Kippur, and why Tashlich is said by running water: to show Hashem we will never take our sins back.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for the Ten Days of Teshuvah. Uncle Yossi explains that these days, from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, prepare us for the holiest day of the year, when Hashem forgives us and grants a good and sweet year. Our part is teshuvah: being extra careful in our thoughts, our speech and our deeds. He recalls going to Tashlich after Mincha on Rosh Hashanah, at an ocean, river, lake or well, and asks why it must be living, moving water. Real teshuvah means deciding firmly never to repeat the sin, and Hashem knows what is in our hearts. A paper dropped on the floor can be picked up again, but a paper thrown into moving water floats away for good. That is how we show Hashem our sins are gone forever. We come back from Tashlich singing and dancing, trusting that we will be sealed for a good year on Yom Kippur.
display.lesson: Real teshuvah means deciding never to do the wrong thing again, like throwing something into moving water that you can never get back.
